baseline_verse.text: But Yahweh is the true God[a]; he is the living God and the everlasting King. At his wrath the earth quakes[c][b], and the nations cannot endure his indignation.

footnotes.text: Hebrew: 'And the LORD'; the conjunction may also be read simply as connective, but here it likely carries a contrast with the idols described in the surrounding context.
Or 'God of truth.' The phrase likely means 'the true God' in contrast to false gods.

The shorter Greek text represented by Codex Vaticanus lacks verses 6–8 and 10 and places the material of verse 9 within verse 5. A published reconstruction of the fragmentary Hebrew manuscript 4Q71 supports this arrangement. Another ancient Hebrew manuscript, 4Q70, preserves part of verse 10; a form of this verse also appears in the margin of the Greek manuscript Codex Marchalianus. This translation retains the longer Hebrew form; which form is earlier remains unsettled.
